changes.headline: Overnight fade on the Russia sanctions waiver, against a physically bullish weekend
changes.dek: Brent Dec26 $107.88 (-1.80 percent) and WTI Nov26 $100.25 (-1.14 percent) at about 04:27 GMT (Reuters), from Friday settles of $109.86 and $101.41.. The overnight session eased in steps after the United States waived the Graham Act sanctions and duties on Russia on Oct 16, before their Oct 18 start. Market commentary named the waiver and profit-taking after a week in which WTI gained 10.4 percent. The physical board pointed the other way all weekend: Gulf crude flows stepped down, Ukraine struck St. Petersburg in a very large drone wave, and a further mine strike was claimed in Hormuz late Sunday without independent confirmation. No Russian diesel loading has been reported under the waiver, and Moscow's export ban runs through October.
changes.balance_read: The market faded a physically bullish weekend on a legal signature: policy loosened while physical supply tightened, and the two only connect when barrels load. Monday's close and the first loading report decide which side was pricing reality.
changes.publishers: Reuters, Oct 19, 2026 (overnight marks; market commentary); Reuters and White House text summaries, Oct 16 to 17, 2026 (waiver order; diesel arrangement)

changes.headline: Gulf crude flows step down to about 8.5 Mb/d; Riyadh airport reopened Sunday
changes.dek: Kpler Friday note via Reuters: about 8.5 Mb/d on a seven-day average last week, at least 10 confirmed vessel incidents. King Khalid airport reopened Oct 18, was suspended again for several hours on Sunday on a fresh GACA announcement, and was gradually resuming.. Kpler's Gulf flows series differs from the Hormuz shipments and clearance prints published last week (9.4 Mb/d and 11.62 Mb/d); the measures are not the same and every vintage since mid-October points down. The IRGC claim of a further mine strike late Sunday is unnamed and unconfirmed, and the maritime coordination body described the Oct 17 claims as unsubstantiated. In Riyadh, the airport reopened Sunday after its closure notice expired, GACA then suspended it again for several hours the same day, and flights were gradually resuming; foreign carriers return on staggered schedules and a regional airspace warning still runs to Dec 10.
changes.balance_read: Confirmed incidents and flow prints keep stepping down while claims outrun verification; the one infrastructure normalization of the weekend is an airport, not a barrel. The flow series, not the claim count, remains the tradeable input.
changes.publishers: Reuters, Oct 19, 2026 (Kpler Friday note); Reuters republication and Iranian state media, Oct 18 to 19, 2026 (mine claim, unverified); Riyadh reopening reporting, Oct 18 to 19, 2026

changes.headline: Diesel crack closed below $100 on Friday; Monday's close decides the break
changes.dek: Diesel crack $99.35 on the completed Oct 16 close (validated history refreshed Oct 19); 3-2-1 crack $55.15; streak above $100 ended at nine days; 37 total days above $100; maximum $117.92 (Sep 16).. Friday was the first completed close below $100 after the nine-day streak. The physical facts did not improve over the weekend: Ryazan CDU-6 remains suspended, the St. Petersburg terminal and depot damage is unassessed, and no Russian diesel cargo has been reported loaded. The policy variable changed instead: the sanctions waiver keeps the licensed channel for Russian-origin diesel open. A second close below $100 alongside published IEA arrival timing or a US distillate build would confirm the regime break; a close back above $100 reopens the streak question.
changes.balance_read: The crack broke its streak on the completed close before the waiver could move a barrel, so the break is a price fact and the waiver is still a probability. Arrivals, loadings, and the Wednesday distillate line are the evidence that converts either way.
changes.publishers: Validated crack history, refreshed Oct 19, 2026; Reuters, Oct 16, 2026 (Ryazan unit suspension; AAA retail diesel)

flags.title: Hormuz flows at about 8.5 Mb/d; mine claims unverified
flags.detail: Kpler puts Gulf crude flows at about 8.5 Mb/d on a seven-day average last week, with at least 10 confirmed vessel incidents. The IRGC has now claimed three mine strikes since Friday; none has a named vessel or independent confirmation, the Oct 17 claims were described as unsubstantiated by the maritime coordination body, and CENTCOM says 97 percent of vessels seeking transit have passed safely. Iran's seven-day plan via Qatar has produced no published terms. Trade the confirmed incident count and the flow prints, not the claims. Trigger: A confirmed new vessel incident, a Kpler flow print stepping down again, or independent confirmation of any mine claim

flags.title: Sanctions waiver: the diesel channel is open on paper, not yet in barrels
flags.detail: The Oct 16 executive order waived the Graham Act sanctions, restrictions and duties under the Section 115 national-interest waiver, with up to 60 days to assess the impact per the Secretary of State. The announced diesel arrangement totals about 4.8 million tons across four tranches, and the import licence stands. Still missing: a reported loading, a named buyer, and a shipment schedule, with Moscow's export ban running through October and the Baltic refining and export system struck on Oct 17 to 18. The waiver raises the probability the barrels eventually move; it does not schedule them. Trigger: A reported Russian diesel loading, a named buyer, or a move in Congress to block the arrangement

flags.title: November apportionment due today; December's marker settled on one lot
flags.detail: WCS Dec26 settled at -$27.40 (ICE TMW settle, Oct 16) on 1 lot, the widest print of the episode, while the January to June tenors widened $1.05 to $1.20 on traded volume. October apportionment stands at 8 percent lights and 4 percent heavies at Kerrobert. The November notice, expected Oct 19, had not been published as of this edition and is the print that tests whether the winter-wide strip is underwritten by nominations or by positioning. Trigger: Publication of the November Mainline apportionment notice, or the next ICE file settling December on real volume

flags.title: Freight wall: Western heavies reprice together
flags.detail: The latest Baltic weekly (week ending Oct 9, pulled Oct 16) has TD9 (Caribbean to US Gulf Coast) at WS 1030, about $19.08/bbl estimated and up 51 percent on the week, TD28 (Vancouver to China) at $25.58/bbl, up 85 percent, and the USGC to China VLCC leg at $40.23/bbl against a Friday Brent-WTI settle spread of $8.45. High Caribbean to Gulf freight makes competing heavy sellers captive to the Gulf, so their length is offered at deeper FOB discounts and pressures WCS Houston pricing whether it fills or not. The failed snap-back stands: Joliet restarted weeks ago and the differential did not rebound. Trigger: A fresh competing-grade FOB discount print, a TD9 move of 20 percent or more, or a WCS Houston response to a freight turn

forward_calendar.detail: A genuine information print: nobody knows the percentages until Enbridge publishes. October was 8 percent lights / 4 percent heavies at Kerrobert. December TMW settled at -$27.40 on Oct 16 (ICE, 1 lot) ahead of it.

forward_calendar.detail: Production should rebound mechanically after the hurricane shut-in week (13,679 kb/d in the last print). The distillate line arbitrates whether the diesel crack's close below $100 is a regime break.

forward_calendar.what: Syncrude return verdict (SYN Nov26) and next COT vintage
forward_calendar.detail: SYN Nov26 settled at +$7.57 on Oct 16 after the coker window wrapped. The pre-registered lines are +$7.00 (premium was priced for the return, or the return slipped) and +$6.50 (supply-return read confirmed). The COT vintage as of Oct 20 is the first that can show whether Friday's escalation buying was short covering or new length.

The DNR's formal Notice of Violation of Oct 13 reaches its enforcement conference. Line 5 is operating via its temporary bypass; the conference is a regulatory-track event for the reroute, not a flow event today.
